summary: Regional latency spike: cross-region routing (us-east -> eu-west) causing timeouts and elevated P95
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-03 10:15 UTC, Acme Analytics observed a sudden increase in generation latency and intermittent request timeouts. Impact: Customer traffic originating in us-east was routed to eu-west, increasing RTT and causing user-visible P95 latency to rise from ~220ms to ~1.8s and some 504s/timeouts on long-running streaming requests. Environment: prod / us-east (customer region pinned to us-east but routing showed cross-region egress).
impact: Multiple production inference endpoints reported P95 latency regression and ~0.8% 5xx rate for affected routes. Business impact: customer dashboards degraded and critical product workflows delayed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send inference request to customer endpoint in us-east with streaming enabled and long context (>1024 tokens).
2) Observe increased initial token latency and occasional streaming disconnects after ~10-30s.
3) Verify request trace shows hops leaving us-east and landing in eu-west region nodes.
logs: Proxy logs (router-1): 2026-03-03T10:17:02Z - route selected: eu-west-1 for customer acme-123 (affinity_score=0.42)
LB logs: healthcheck pass count decreased in us-east pool starting 10:12 UTC, weight rebalancing triggered
Application logs (serving runtime): 2026-03-03T10:18:10Z - kv-cache-miss spike; increased GC and token generation stalls
investigation_notes: 10:20 UTC - Initial triage by support: customer requests from us-east were observed with backend region tag eu-west in traces.
10:30 UTC - SRE oncall (Arjun Kapoor) confirmed a rolling config change to smart-routing weights that started at 10:10 UTC and coincides with spike.

10:45 UTC - Hypothesis: Weight rebalancer considered us-east pool under-healthchecked (transient failure) and shifted traffic to eu-west; affinity algorithm then failed to reassign back due to stale region affinity cache.
11:05 UTC - Confirmed router service had an off-by-one bug in region affinity TTL resulting in 30m stale affinity entries after a recent deployment (PR #452).
11:30 UTC - Temporary mitigation: forced weight restoration for us-east pool and cleared affinity cache for affected customer set; P95 returned to baseline ~11:40 UTC.
12:00 UTC - Engineering rollback of the faulty affinity TTL change deployed: reverted PR #452; added additional telemetry to catch affinity cache misses.
comments: Maya Chen (Support): 2026-03-03 10:22 - Customer reports spike in P95 and some 504s. They are on a dedicated us-east pool. Please prioritize.
Arjun Kapoor (SRE): 2026-03-03 10:35 - Investigating routing weight changes. Saw rebalancer events at 10:12-10:15 that drained us-east capacity and diverted traffic.
Liam Patel (Support): 2026-03-03 11:20 - Applied affinity cache clear for acme-123 and manually restored weights for us-east. Observed P95 drop back to ~240ms.
Arjun Kapoor (SRE): 2026-03-03 12:05 - Deployed rollback of the affinity-ttl change (reverted PR #452). Monitoring for regressions.
Customer (Acme Engineering): 2026-03-03 12:30 - Confirmed service responsiveness restored for affected endpoints; thanks for the fast response.
resolution: Root cause: recent change to smart-routing affinity TTL (PR #452) introduced stale region affinity entries which, combined with transient healthcheck noise in the us-east pool, caused the rebalancer to divert traffic to eu-west. Fix: reverted the TTL change and patched the affinity cache logic to fall back to regional pinning on repeated healthcheck flaps. Mitigation: cleared affinity cache for affected customers and manually restored us-east pool weights. Follow-ups: add unit test for affinity TTL, add alert for cross-region hop rate >0.5% for customer-scoped traffic, and postmortem and runbook update.
resolution_notes: Mitigation performed: 2026-03-03 11:30 UTC - cleared affinity cache and restored weights
Monitoring: Increased sampling of cross-region hops for 72 hours; dashboard and alert created: cross_region_hop_rate_customer > 0.5%
